programme.title: Solar System
programme.desc: The host of the program, Professor Brian Cox, presents selected information about the solar system.Viewers will learn about planets and moons covered with volcanoes that erupt with fire and ice.In the following parts, the scientist talks about the most interesting atmospheric conditions that were noticed on celestial bodies neighboring the Earth.He visits landscapes created by dust whirls, mountains covered with metallic frost and monsoon rains on one of the moons.In addition, Professor Cox will introduce viewers to frozen regions of the solar system, including a dwarf planet with mountains of solid ice floating on it, as well as a black and white moon.

programme.title: Joanna Lumley's Spice Trail Adventure
programme.desc: Actress Joanna Lumley, known from the films "Absolutely Fabulous" and "The Wolf of Wall Street", goes on an expedition to discover the origins of spices.It follows two continents in the footsteps of pharaohs, crusaders and rulers.He visits the Indonesian Banda Islands, which were once the only place on Earth where nutmeg grew.He also visits Madagascar, the place of the largest vanilla cultivation.It also goes to India and the Middle East.He realizes that for hundreds of years, the East and the West have been linked by the spice trade.

programme.title: World's Most Amazing Walks
programme.desc: Robson Green gained popularity, among others, thanks to the role of an experienced detective in the crime series "Grantchester".Privately, the actor is a great lover of hiking and fishing.The new series documents eight expeditions along selected tourist routes in Europe.The artist traveled, among others, the northern coast of Normandy, following in the footsteps of soldiers taking part in a key battle of World War II.On the Trail of the Eagles' Nests in Poland, he had the opportunity to admire impressive landscapes and the ruins of medieval castles.A monument to a bygone era. Robson Green begins exploring the most beautiful trekking routes in the world in his native Great Britain.Hadrian's Wall is one of the most important monuments of ancient Rome on the Islands.The trail, divided into stages, is 135 kilometers long.It has special meaning for the actor because he grew up in this area.He follows familiar paths through the rugged moors.He has loved this landscape since childhood.He is amazed not only by nature, but also by the heritage of the past.He gets to know, among other things, Vindolanda - a Roman camp built in the 1st century.Archaeologists still make discoveries here related to the times of the Roman Empire.

programme.title: The Green Planet
programme.desc: The creators of the production invite viewers on a journey through the lush world of plants.It hides many surprising phenomena and hundreds of amazing heroes.Thanks to the lenses of specialized cameras, the mysterious life of nature's creations will be shown up close.Scientific research shows that nature is a perfect system of connecting vessels.In each of the five episodes, we will learn about a different group of plants and the secrets of their survival.The creators will talk about, among others:stories about seeds that can survive civilizations, trees that take care of each other, and creatures of nature that are as aggressive and spontaneous as animals.We will also learn about the relationships between people and animals with plants.It turns out that plants count, hunt, cheat, communicate, protect their relatives and manipulate animals for their own purposes.Contrary to appearances, when plants and animals interact with each other, it is usually the plant that sets the tone of the relationship.The series' narrator will be Sir David Attenborough, a popularizer of natural science Viewers will discover the world of aquatic plants.They create some of the most beautiful and important habitats on Earth.Life in water is not easy, which is why individual plant species have found innovative ways to survive.The color-changing algae that grows on the Rainbow River in Colombia sticks to rocks thanks to a natural version of superglue.In the Brazilian Pantanal, plants fight for light using air bags.Their goal is to stay afloat and reproduce quickly.The globe seaweed, which comes from Japan, uses the water currents of Lake Akan to move to an ideal place for development.During the flowering period, aquatic plants behave like terrestrial plants for a time, displaying flowers into the air on stiff stems.Only one flowering plant has reached the sea and forms underwater communities - seagrass.Its submerged savannahs not only support large numbers of animals, but also sequester carbon dioxide 35 times faster than tropical forests.Now under threat, they are crucial in the fight against climate change.
